title: Gravity & Mass
source: Science G3 B1 Study sheet pp.48-50, Worksheet Q8, Q10-Q11

scenes.t: If you hold a pencil and let it go, it falls down to the floor. Why doesn't it go up to the ceiling? Because of gravity!
Gravity is a force that pulls things down towards the center of the Earth. It keeps everything on Earth.
Without gravity, there would be no water in the seas, and people and animals could not live on Earth.
The Moon has gravity too. Rocks in space called meteors are pulled to the Moon and crash, leaving holes called craters.
Scientists think a very large meteor hit the Earth long ago, changed the climate and killed the dinosaurs.
Mass is how much stuff is in an object. We measure it in grams with a scale.
If an apple has a mass of 200 grams and we cut it into pieces, all the pieces together still have a mass of 200 grams.
If we squeeze 50 grams of clay, it still has a mass of 50 grams. Breaking or squashing does not change the total mass!

items.a: A force that pulls things down towards the center of the Earth.
A hole left when a meteor hits the Moon.
How much stuff is in an object.
Parts added together = mass of the whole object.
A giant meteor may have caused their extinction.

activities.title: Memory: Gravity & Mass

activities.title: Mass Detective
activities.prompt: Does the total mass CHANGE or STAY THE SAME?

why.s: Cutting, breaking or squashing does not change the total mass.
why.c: Adding or taking away stuff changes the mass.

items: putting pencils back in the case

activities.title: The Apple Scale Test
activities.goal: Prove that the parts add up to the whole mass.
activities.safe: An adult must cut the apple.

predict.q: Will the pieces together weigh the same as the whole apple?

steps.t: Put the plate on the scale and press zero. Weigh the whole apple and write the mass.
Ask an adult to cut the apple into 4 pieces.
Weigh each piece on its own and write each mass.
Add the four masses together and compare with the whole apple.

activities.result: The four pieces added together have the same mass as the whole apple (maybe 1 gram less from the juice).
activities.why: Cutting does not add or remove stuff, so the total mass stays the same.
